hints.title: Lane Stage Decomposition
hints.text: Model Mario journey as progressing through at most three stages across the two lanes.

hints.title: Multi-State Invariant
hints.text: Stage 0 is driving in lane 1 with 0 switches. Stage 1 is driving in lane 2 with 1 switch. Stage 2 is driving in lane 1 with 2 switches.

hints.title: Kadane Running Transitions
hints.text: Maintain running maximum sums for each stage. Mario can start at any mile marker and exit at any mile marker.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxCoins(self, lane1: list[int], lane2: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(lane1)
        ans = -float('inf')
        dp0 = -float('inf')
        dp1 = -float('inf')
        dp2 = -float('inf')
        for i in range(n):
            c1, c2 = lane1[i], lane2[i]
            new_dp0 = max(c1, dp0 + c1)
            new_dp1 = max(c2, dp0 + c2, dp1 + c2)
            new_dp2 = max(dp1 + c1, dp2 + c1)
            dp0, dp1, dp2 = new_dp0, new_dp1, new_dp2
            ans = max(ans, dp0, dp1, dp2)
        return ans
```

variables: n: length of freeway lane arrays
complexity.notes: Single pass maintaining running maximum sums across at most three lane stages.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all possible trip start and end indices and lane-switch mile markers is O(n^3).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Kadane-like multi-state DP tracks optimal subarray sums across the 3 lane stages simultaneously.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize that at most 2 lane switches constrain the path to at most 3 alternating lane stages.
